h1: El Paso County Justice of the Peace Court Ticket Lawyer
intro: If a Sheriff's deputy, DPS trooper or constable wrote your ticket, it is filed in one of the El Paso County Justice of the Peace precincts — not downtown Municipal Court. Attorney Robert Navar handles every JP precinct for a flat $69.
summary: El Paso County Justice of the Peace (JP) courts handle Class C traffic citations written by the Sheriff's Office, DPS state troopers and county constables, organized by precinct across the county.

There are JP precincts serving downtown, the Northeast, the Lower Valley and Socorro area, Horizon and the East, the Westside, and Anthony and Canutillo — your citation lists the precinct where it was filed.
Our flat fee for any JP court is $69 per citation, with discounted add-ons for extra tickets from the same stop. Hire online or call 915-503-1600.
JP courts offer deferred disposition and defensive-driving dismissals, but each judge runs the docket differently — we know the habits of each precinct.
In most JP cases you never appear; we file the appearance and negotiate with the county attorney's prosecutor on your behalf.

sections.heading: Who Writes the Tickets That Land in JP Court
paragraphs: The Justice of the Peace courts are El Paso County's courts, which means they receive citations from county and state officers rather than city police. The three big sources are the El Paso County Sheriff's Office, which patrols unincorporated areas like Montana Vista, the Upper Valley, Canutillo and the stretches of Montana Ave and Loop 375 outside city limits; the Texas Department of Public Safety, whose state troopers work I-10, US-54, Highway 20 and the rural highways toward Fabens and Tornillo; and the county constables, who write tickets in their own precincts and serve court papers.

If the citation header says "Sheriff," "DPS" or "Constable," you are in JP court. City of El Paso police tickets go to El Paso Municipal Court, and tickets from Horizon City, Socorro, San Elizario, Clint, Anthony and Vinton police go to those cities' own municipal courts. The precinct number should also appear on the citation; if it is unclear, our free ticket and warrant lookup will locate it.

sections.heading: How the JP Precincts Are Organized Across El Paso County
paragraphs: El Paso County divides its Justice of the Peace courts by precinct, and most precincts have more than one judge. Broadly, there are JP offices downtown near the county courthouse, in the Northeast, in the Lower Valley and Socorro area, out east toward Horizon City, on the Westside, and in the Anthony and Canutillo area serving the Upper Valley. Each office keeps its own docket calendar and clerk procedures. Verify the current address and docket schedule with the specific precinct before you go anywhere — or hire us and skip the trip.

That geography matters because a JP case is filed where the stop happened, not where you live. A Northeast resident ticketed by a trooper on I-10 near Anthony will have a case in the Anthony/Canutillo-area precinct, a half-hour drive each way. Robert Navar's office handles all of the precincts.

JP courts are also the courts that hear county warrants. A missed JP appearance date produces a warrant and a separate failure-to-appear charge the same way Municipal Court does, and the county reports those cases to the state's OMNI hold program, which blocks your license renewal at DPS.

sections.heading: What a JP Docket Looks Like and Who Prosecutes
paragraphs: Traffic cases in JP court are prosecuted by the El Paso County Attorney's office, which assigns prosecutors to the precinct dockets. Compared with Municipal Court, JP dockets are smaller and move faster, and the judge is more likely to be personally involved in the pretrial discussion. That is a plus when the defense has something to say — a defective citation, a transferred officer, a missing calibration record — because the decision-maker is in the room.

When we file an appearance, the court sets the case on a pretrial or announcement docket. Robert Navar or a member of our staff attends, confers with the county attorney's prosecutor, and negotiates. Our goals are the same ones listed in the how to fight a ticket in El Paso guide: dismissal first, deferred disposition second, a non-moving reduction when nothing else is available. If the trooper or deputy does not appear for a trial setting, we ask for a dismissal on the spot.

sections.heading: Trooper Tickets: What Makes JP Cases Different
paragraphs: A large share of JP traffic cases come from DPS troopers, and trooper tickets have their own features. Troopers write for higher speeds on the interstate, so 25-mph-over citations — which most courts will not resolve with defensive driving — are common. They also write many no insurance and expired registration tickets at checkpoints and on the US-54 corridor. And because DPS troopers are transferred around the state, the officer named on a year-old citation is often no longer available to testify, which is real leverage for a dismissal.

Commercial drivers get special attention in JP court. Trooper tickets on I-10 frequently involve CDL holders, who are barred by federal rules from deferred disposition and masking. For those clients we focus on the citation's defects and on negotiating a charge that does not count as a serious violation under the CDL rules. Tell us at intake if you hold a CDL — it changes the plan.

sections.heading: Our $69 Flat Fee for Any El Paso County JP Precinct
paragraphs: We charge $69 per citation in every El Paso County Justice of the Peace precinct. The fee is a little higher than our $59 Municipal Court rate because JP precincts are spread across the county and the dockets require travel, but it is flat: no hourly billing, no surprise charges. Extra citations from the same stop are $10–$30 add-ons at checkout. If a warrant already exists, we add $35 for the first warrant and $20 for each additional one and handle the recall together with the ticket.

A JP speeding conviction adds two points and three years of higher premiums; the $69 fee is typically recovered many times over by the first renewal that does not show a ticket. The consultation is free, se habla español, and we can usually tell you within a few minutes what to expect in your precinct.

sections.heading: Before Your JP Court Date
paragraphs: Check the appearance date and the precinct on the citation, do not pay it, and do not mail in a defensive-driving request on your own — that is a plea and it removes most of our leverage. Hire us online or call 915-503-1600 before the date; if it has already passed, call anyway and we will deal with the warrant first.
This page is general information, not legal advice about your case. Precinct practices change, so verify the current docket schedule with the court or let our office confirm it for you.

faqs.q: How do I know my ticket is in a JP court and which precinct?
faqs.a: Look at the issuing agency on the citation. Sheriff's Office, DPS and constable tickets go to a Justice of the Peace court, and the precinct is usually printed on the ticket. If it isn't, our free ticket and warrant lookup will find it.

faqs.q: How much is a lawyer for a JP court ticket in El Paso County?
faqs.a: Our flat fee is $69 per citation in any El Paso County JP precinct. Additional citations from the same stop are discounted add-ons, and warrants are $35 for the first and $20 for each additional one.

faqs.q: Do I have to drive out to the precinct office?
faqs.a: Usually not. We file the appearance and attend the pretrial docket for you, whether the precinct is downtown, in Anthony or out toward Horizon. You would only need to appear if the case went to trial, which is rare.

faqs.q: Will a JP judge grant deferred disposition?
faqs.a: Most JP judges in El Paso County grant deferred disposition under art. 45.051 for ordinary moving violations. High-speed cases, CDL holders and repeat offenders face more resistance, and those are the cases where an attorney's request carries more weight than a driver's.

faqs.q: A trooper wrote me a ticket on I-10 months ago and I forgot about it. Is there a warrant?
faqs.a: Very likely, plus a possible OMNI hold on your license renewal. Call us the same day. We file an appearance, ask the JP court to recall the warrant and put the ticket back on a docket — see traffic warrant recall.

faqs.q: Do you handle tickets in the Anthony and Canutillo area precinct?
faqs.a: Yes. We handle every El Paso County JP precinct, including the Upper Valley offices serving Anthony, Canutillo and Vinton, and the Lower Valley offices serving Socorro, San Elizario, Clint and Fabens.
